label: Rock in Rio 2026 — 13/09 (dom) · Gramado
_note_supply: On sale at the box office when observed 2026-09-01. Cheapest Gramado R$ 275,00 -- tied with 04/09 as the cheapest of the seven nights.
_note_face_value: Gramado face value (Juan, 2026-09-01): Inteira R$ 870,00 / Meia R$ 435,00. Because the gate does not check class, R$ 435,00 is the effective benchmark for the cheapest usable ticket -- anything above it is a resale premium. Documentation only: no rule reads this field.
_note_filters: Gramado only (Juan's call 2026-09-01). entry_class is deliberately unfiltered: Rock in Rio does not check ticket type at the gate, so any class is usable and the cheapest one wins. Set extra.sector to null to watch all 6 sectors.
_note_rules: ONLY lowest_ever is enabled. lowest_in_window is configured but DISABLED here: these are tracking nights, not nights Juan would buy, so an expiring-baseline rule would add alerts he cannot act on. Flip `enabled` to arm it.
_note_critical_price: critical_price is the anomaly floor, and it does TWO jobs from one number. (1) Any price under it alerts immediately -- on entering the band and on each new low inside it -- bypassing the 6h window entirely. (2) Nothing under it ever becomes a baseline for lowest_ever or lowest_in_window, so a mispricing cannot ratchet them shut. This is not hypothetical: on 2026-09-02T13:46Z a single R$ 66,00 Gramado || Inteira, present for one run and gone the next minute, took the lowest_ever record on 04/09 -- which has no expiry, so the rule was permanently dead on the night it was built for. X is set just under this night's observed floor (R$ 275,00), because a price that far below trading range is far more likely to be a listing error than a deal. The exclusion is applied on READ, so arming this heals a history that is already poisoned.
_note_buy: Read ONLY by the sibling tool knowledge/projects/ticket-autobuy; price-watcher never reads this key and never buys. AUTO-BUY armed 2026-09-02 on Juan's call: all 7 nights, ceiling R$200,00, ONE reservation per night ever. ⛔ min_price_brl is deliberately ABSENT -- Juan chose to buy a suspiciously cheap row rather than refuse it (an unpaid hold on a mispricing costs nothing, and refusing it misses the one dip the tool exists for). That is the opposite of price-watcher's critical_price, which still excludes sub-R$200 rows from BASELINES -- two different jobs for the same number, do not collapse them. ⏰ The runner only fires 10:00-04:00 BRT and disarms this block the moment it buys, so `enabled: true` here means 'armed', never 'will buy repeatedly'.
